extracted.intended_audience: U.S. citizens (current students and recent graduates) and other prospective applicants considering the Fulbright U.S. Student Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility criteria for applying to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program, including who may apply (current students, recent graduates, artists), which award types are available, where/how to submit an application, and relevant deadlines. Also directs other applicant types (professors, non-U.S. citizens, highly experienced professionals) to the appropriate Fulbright channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Current U.S. Student
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there. Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. Citizen but not a Student
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying. Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. The 'Getting Started' page provides information on eligibility and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Artist / Creative & Performing Arts candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arts candidates for the U.S. Student Program should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less). Artists with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Classification — Creative & Performing Arts fall under Study/Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These projects are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / Process — U.S. Professors and Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support your students in applying for a U.S. Student Program award, please connect with the Fulbright Program Adviser at your institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / Process — Non-U.S. Citizens (applying to the United States)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a non-U.S. citizen interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States, you will need to apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in your home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find out more information on the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program via your local commission or embassy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Experience Expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-enrolled applicants and arts candidates should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields in which they are applying (typically 7 years or less).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with more extensive professional experience are advised to consider the Fulbright Scholar Program instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Types Available
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple award types are available under the U.S. Student Program, including Study/Research Awards, English Teaching Assistant Awards, Fulbright-National Geographic Award Program, and Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award opportunities are open in all academic disciplines, including the creative and performing arts. Specific application components and program details are on linked pages (e.g., Study/Research: Academic; ETA; Fulbright-National Geographic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Where and how you apply depends on applicant status: current U.S. students apply through their institution; non-U.S. citizens apply through a Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy; professors/administrators apply via fulbrightscholars.org for Scholar Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect with your Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA) on campus for guidance and use the 'Start Application' and 'Search FPA' links provided on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and Competition Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition cycles have defined application periods and deadlines (example: 2027–2028 Competition is open; National Deadline: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition timelines vary by cycle (e.g., 2026–2027 Application: Closed; Final Notification: Rolling basis through spring). Applicants should consult the site for the current cycle dates and begin applications early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Support Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The program provides resources such as webinars, tutorials, application tips, and an online application portal to support applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed include webinars on Statement of Grant Purpose and alumni panels. Use 'Find an Adviser', 'Upcoming Webinars', and 'Fulbright Online Application' to access support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on Appropriate Program Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should choose the program that matches their qualifications and career stage (U.S. Student Program vs. Fulbright Scholar Program vs. other Fulbright tracks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site repeatedly advises those with a Ph.D. or significant professional experience to consider the Fulbright Scholar Program and directs non-U.S. citizens to country-specific Fulbright Commission/E embassy pathways.
